name: Page Industries Ltd
about: Incorporated in 1995, Page Industries Limited is the exclusive licensee of JOCKEY International Inc. for manufacturing, distribution, and marketing of the JOCKEY® brand in India, Sri Lanka, Bangladesh, Nepal, and the UAE. Page Industries is also the exclusive licensee of Speedo International Ltd. for the manufacturing, marketing, and distribution of the Speedo brand in India.

statements.text: Revenue compounded 13.1% a year over 5 years (FY21→FY26); profit after tax 17.5%.
EBITDA margin expanded 340 bps over 5 years (18.6% → 22.0%).
Revenue growth accelerated from 6% to 12% YoY over the last 4 quarters.
Over 5 years: ₹3,170 cr of profit, ₹3,403 cr of operating cash — conversion 1.07x.

context.speaker: Deepanjan B.
context.text: Thank you, V.S.G. Good afternoon, everyone, and welcome to today's call. Let me take you through the financial performance for the second quarter of FY 2027 and of the first half. Quarter two FY 2027 performance, sales volume was 59.8 million pieces, which is a growth of 5.5% over Q2 last year. Sales value was INR14,396.1 million, up 11.5%, helped by the 2.5% price increase, which was fully affected in the quarter. EBITDA was INR3,001.4 million, up 7.4%. EBITDA margin was 20.8% as against 21.7% last year. Cotton and crude-led raw materials remained elevated, and the price increase only partially cushioned this pressure. The margin stayed healthy and within our planned range of 19%-21%. Profit after tax was INR2,025.4 million, a growth of 4% over Q2 last year. Coming to the first half performance, sales volume was 121.7 million pieces, up 5.6%. Sales value was INR 28,600.6 million, a growth of 9.7% over H1 last year. EBITDA was INR5,891.4 million, up 2.6%. EBITDA margin was 20.6% as against 22% in the same period last year, reflecting the cost inflation. Profit after tax was INR3,953.5 million, broadly in line with first half last year. Coming to the balance sheet items, inventory days stood at 74.0 at the end of Q2, as against 74.8 at the beginning of current financial year. Net working capital days improved to 51.3 days from 55.9 days at the beginning of the current financial year. With that, we can now take up questions.

context.speaker: Videesha Sheth
context.text: Hi. Both my questions were pertaining to the earlier discussion only. One on the volume growth. When we look at the remaining part of FY 2027, the ask becomes as steep as 14%-15% odd. So Karthik, if you could please help us out as to how should we think about the building blocks or the moving parts as to how would you land up attaining that growth in the second half? One, of course, would be the timing shift of festivals, but if you could help us understand the same.

context.speaker: Karthik Yathindra
context.text: Sure. Yes, as we see it, the asking rate for H2, as you pointed out, is about 14% in volume growth to hit a double-digit number. Basically, three levers in terms of what will be different in H2 when compared to H1. One is obviously the build-up to the festive season has moved from September to October. This is both. Since we are largely a B2B company in terms of what we publish, the primary performance, that build-up will be realized in the month of October, November, as against what we realized in September. Both for a shift in festive, also in the online space, the build-up for the large fests that happens across large marketplaces during the festive season. These two pieces are large impacts. The second one is in terms of a few key new introductions that has been planned for Diwali. That is largely going to be realized in the month of October and November. These are key categories in men's innerwear as well as bras, which is also backed by campaigns, marketing campaigns, and investments. These are largely the building blocks. Otherwise, from a tertiary point of view, I think we are well on course against what we have planned even in H1. The large impact that we are seeing is largely in primary because of this shift. Hence the confidence of being able to recover that 14% asking rate for H2.

As regards our transformation journey, it is moving ahead steadily. The S/4HANA implementation is progressing well, with go-live planned to happen during the Q4 of this financial year. The scale-up of our Distribution Management System is also on track. Our initiative to strengthen cybersecurity and our HR transformation program remain firmly on course. Together, these investments are aimed at making us a more agile and resilient organization, better equipped to serve our consumers and retail partners.

No, I think the headcount has been optimal, but going forward, the headcount will go up as we ramp up Odisha operations as well as K.R. Pete two operations. So, what you have seen in H1 is more the ramp-up phase, which will have to accelerate a lot more in H2. So, by the sheer increase in headcount, you will see manpower cost in a way catching up on the business. As far Page 6 of 15 Page Industries Limited November 12, 2026 as wage increase is concerned, as of now, a large portion of our wage increase impact is in Karnataka, which has been affected from April itself, and that has been well accounted in what we have published in H1.

Well, for both the units, we are on track as far as plan is concerned, and the complete ramp-up will take another 1.5 year . I think we will, in a way, reach our peak capacity by end of next financial year. As of now, we are operating at about 40% of where we want to be, or not where we want to be, where we can get to as far as these two plants are concerned. I would imagine by end of next financial year is where we will be hitting peak capacity utilization, as far as these two plants are concerned.

Hi, thanks for giving me another opportunity on the follow-up. Just taking it from Jignesh and Rishi during the call. Now we are gunning for a target of double-digit volume growth, and this was at the start of the year. Then I am just not able to understand how exactly are we not prepared for this ramp-up issue that we faced, given that these are fairly new factories which will take time to ramp up, and we technically, logically being the organization that we are, should have been ready for this in terms of our outsourcing capabilities. Your thoughts on this? Page 14 of 15 Page Industries Limited November 12, 2026

Yeah. So the DMS is underway, but we've not yet completely moved ahead. It's still a very small portion of distributors who are on DMS today. But the goal is by end of this year or latest first quarter of next year, all of the distributors in our network should be on DMS and then give it about a quarter more to stabilize as a tool and thereafter you will start seeing efficiencies coming into the system.

narrative_vs_numbers.claim: EBITDA margin will stay within 19-21% for FY27 despite input-cost inflation (C3, G1).
narrative_vs_numbers.reality: H1 FY27 margin 20.6% (Q1 20.4%, Q2 20.8%), inside the band, though Q2 is down 90 bps YoY from 21.7%.

narrative_vs_numbers.claim: 'The annual goal remains unchanged... double-digit growth in volume' (G2), with revenue also targeted back at double digits (G11).
narrative_vs_numbers.reality: Q1 FY27 volume +5.7% and revenue +7.8%; Q2 revenue +11.5% was partly Q1 billing moved into Q2 (G3). 3-year revenue CAGR is 3.6% vs 13.1% over five years.

narrative_vs_numbers.claim: Input costs had largely normalised by end-June and are expected to stay stable (C3).
narrative_vs_numbers.reality: Q2 FY27 margin recovered only 40 bps QoQ to 20.8%, and PAT grew 4.1% YoY on revenue +11.5%, so profit is lagging sales while margin stays below last year's 21.7%.

narrative_vs_numbers.claim: Working capital tightening: inventory days 73 to 66 and net working capital days 56 to 54 in Q1 FY27 (C1).
narrative_vs_numbers.reality: Consistent with the longer trend: cash conversion cycle 138 days vs 240 three years ago, 5-year CFO/PAT 1.07, ROCE 64%.

bull.point: Margin guidance is dependable: 19-21% restated on four calls (G13, G9, G5, G1), H1 FY27 at 20.6%, and the Q3 FY26 call correctly warned that ~22% would not last (G10).
Capital efficiency: ROCE 64%, 5-year CFO/PAT 1.07, cash conversion cycle cut from 240 to 138 days over three years; borrowings only INR 396 crore (debt/equity 0.26).

Growth is picking up from a low base: revenue +14.1% and +11.5% in two of the last four quarters vs a 3-year CAGR of 3.6%, and the full DMS rollout due by end-FY27 / Q1 FY28 is aimed at distribution efficiencies (C4, G4).

bear.point: Volume goal already behind: Q1 FY27 volume +5.7% vs a double-digit FY27 target (G2, G6), so the remaining quarters need ~11.4%, and Q2's 11.5% revenue growth was flattered by Q1 billing shifted into Q2 (G3).

Margin upside capped by management's own band: TTM margin 21.2% is at the 21% ceiling (G1) and management said ~22% was not sustainable (G10), so PAT growth must come from revenue; Q2 PAT grew only 4.1% on 11.5% revenue growth.

Growth promises are repeated, not delivered: 'near double-digit' (Q2 FY26, G12) and 'double-digit' (Q3 FY26, G11) aspirations carry no date, while 3-year revenue CAGR is 3.6% and 3-year PAT CAGR of 10.2% came largely from +370 bps of margin.

questions: What was Q2 FY27 volume growth, and how much of Q2's 11.5% revenue growth was Q1 billing shifted into Q2 (G3)? In other words, what is underlying H1 growth against the double-digit volume goal (G2)?
Where will the INR 40-50 crore FY27 subsidy (G7) be booked? If it sits inside EBITDA it is worth ~70-90 bps of margin, so what is the 19-21% band excluding it?
What did the Q4 FY26 'close to 5%' target (G8) refer to (marketing spend vs the 4-4.5% FY26 budget in G15, or something else), and how much H1 FY27 spend went toward it?
